xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3924: pipeline-membership: intermittent gh graphql failure surfaces as a toast; capture stderr, retry once; listProjectTrackerIssues is blind to GitHub-tracked projects

plan.title: pipeline-membership: intermittent gh graphql failure surfaces as a toast; capture stderr, retry once; listProjectTrackerIssues is blind to GitHub-tracked projects
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5-1

narratives.Problem: runGitHubGraphql in src/lib/pipeline-membership-gather.ts shells out to `gh api graphql` and, on failure, rethrows execFile's error whose message embeds the 50-alias query and drops stderr. The operator sees `[pipeline-membership] refresh failed for overdeck ... Command failed: gh api graphql ... (forge_unavailable)` intermittently (4x on the 0.51.0 build) and cannot tell why; the same batch succeeds by hand. One transient subprocess failure fails the whole gather with no retry. Separately, listProjectTrackerIssues filters rows with `ref.startsWith(prefix + '-')`, but the GitHub tracker's ref is a bare `#N`, so the function returns nothing for GitHub-tracked projects (latent: the gather only calls it for non-GitHub trackers).
narratives.Proposal: Extract the gh GraphQL runner into a new module src/lib/github-graphql-run.ts with injectable exec and delay. Its error message carries the exit code (or `timeout`), the attempt count, and up to 500 chars of stderr, and never the query. Retry exactly once after 1000 ms when stdout has no JSON envelope; a parsed envelope with usable data is returned (unchanged), and an errors-only envelope throws without retry. Keep gather.ts at or below its origin/main line count (765). Move issueIdFromTrackerIssue from the CLI migrate-plan-home module into src/lib/tracker/issue-id.ts (re-exported from the CLI file), and make listProjectTrackerIssues map rows through a pure exported projectTrackerIssueRows that uses it. The service and routes already keep and serve the last-good snapshot through a failed refresh; pin that with regression tests rather than changing it. Document the retry and last-good behavior in configuration/issue-trackers.mdx and a module header on the gatherer.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Retrying or capturing stderr for the REST `gh api --paginate` path in listOpenPullRequestsSnapshot (gather.ts:62-78).
- Wiring src/lib/github-graphql-cooldown.ts into the gatherer.
- Auto-rescheduling a failed cold (boot-time) membership refresh; periodic-convergence re-gathers within 5 minutes.
- Any change to the frontend ProjectMembershipBoundary alert box.
- Deduplicating the resolveProjectTrackerType copy in migrate-plan-home.ts.
- Making the gather call listTrackerIssues for GitHub-tracked projects (they keep the REST issue lists).
- Fixing the stale docs/PIPELINE-MEMBERSHIP.md pointer in routes/pipeline-membership.ts:7.
- Adding a scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt row for pipeline-membership-gather.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: Retry discriminator: retry once only when gh's stdout is empty or not a JSON envelope; a parsed envelope with non-null data is returned, an errors-only envelope throws immediately.
autoDecisions.rationale: Network failures, gh crashes, and timeouts leave no envelope and are the intermittent class the issue describes; envelope errors (bad query, rate limit) are deterministic and retrying them burns quota. The rule is mechanical and needs no wiring of the unused cooldown module.

autoDecisions.summary: One retry with a fixed 1000 ms delay, no backoff, per-attempt timeout unchanged at 30 s.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for 'retry once'; worst case per chunk is ~61 s in a background refresh, and the settled TTL cache evicts rejections so nothing caches the failure.

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the runner into src/lib/github-graphql-run.ts instead of editing it in place.
autoDecisions.rationale: The file-size ratchet forbids growing gather.ts (765 lines on origin/main), and a module with injectable exec/delay is unit-testable without mocking node:child_process inside the 1361-line gather test, where that mock would also swallow defaultDeps.run and listOpenPullRequestsSnapshot.

autoDecisions.summary: Relocate issueIdFromTrackerIssue to src/lib/tracker/issue-id.ts and re-export it from the CLI module, rather than importing the CLI module from lib as the issue text literally suggests.
autoDecisions.rationale: src/lib importing src/cli/commands is the wrong layering direction and risks the gatherer's import-graph guard test; the re-export keeps the existing CLI test compiling unchanged.

autoDecisions.summary: Treat 'do not surface the banner for a single failed refresh when a last-good snapshot exists' as already satisfied and pin it with regression tests instead of changing server or frontend code.
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified in services/pipeline-membership.ts:94-106 (failure keeps value/refreshedAt) and :117-119 (memberships returned when refreshedAt is set) and routes/pipeline-membership.ts:39-40 and :71-72 (bare array). The observed boot-time banner is the cold-cache case, which the retry reduces and periodic-convergence heals within 5 minutes.

autoDecisions.summary: Error is a plain Error with `cause` set to the original execFile rejection; no new error class.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every consumer (withUnavailableReason, snapshot.lastError, the unavailable body) reads only .message; a class would be speculative surface.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/github-graphql-run.ts per PRD WI-1: export runGitHubGraphql(query, exec = defaultExec, delay = defaultDelay), GhExec/Delay types, GH_GRAPHQL_RETRY_DELAY_MS, GH_GRAPHQL_STDERR_LIMIT, and describeGhGraphqlFailure(error, attempt). defaultExec wraps promisify(execFile)('gh', args, { encoding: 'utf-8', timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 4 MiB }); defaultDelay wraps the global setTimeout in a Promise. In the catch: if the rejection's stdout parses as JSON with a non-null data object, return stdout (existing partial-envelope behavior); otherwise throw new Error(describeGhGraphqlFailure(error, 1), { cause: error }). The message format is `gh api graphql failed (<exit N | timeout>, attempt <n>): <stderr trimmed to 500 chars | no stderr>` and must not include the query. In src/lib/pipeline-membership-gather.ts delete the private runGitHubGraphql (lines 89-114) and import runGitHubGraphql from './github-graphql-run.js'; leave listMergedPullRequestHeadsBatched and listIssueStatesBatched default parameters untouched and keep execFileAsync (still used by listOpenPullRequestsSnapshot and defaultDeps.run). Write tests/unit/lib/github-graphql-run.test.ts with injected exec. Assert message shape ONLY through the pure describeGhGraphqlFailure(error, attempt) (exit code, timeout, 'no stderr', 500-char truncation, no query text), and assert end-to-end runGitHubGraphql behavior only for: success passthrough with the exact gh args, partial envelope returned, and a non-JSON failure rejecting with an Error whose cause is the original rejection and whose message contains 'gh api graphql failed ('. Do not assert an attempt number through runGitHubGraphql in this item — gh-run-retry owns attempt-count assertions so no test is rewritten when the retry loop lands.

items.title: Given the rejection { code: 1, killed: false, stdout: '', stderr: 'error connecting to api.github.com\n' }, describeGhGraphqlFailure(error, 1) returns 'gh api graphql failed (exit 1, attempt 1): error connecting to api.github.com' and the string contains no 'query='

Given the rejection { code: null, killed: true, signal: 'SIGTERM', stdout: '', stderr: '' }, describeGhGraphqlFailure(error, 1) returns 'gh api graphql failed (timeout, attempt 1): no stderr'; given a 600-character stderr, the returned detail contains exactly 500 characters

Given exec rejects with a stdout JSON envelope whose data is a non-null object, runGitHubGraphql returns that stdout string (partial-envelope behavior preserved); given exec resolves, it returns stdout and exec receives ['api','graphql','-f','query=<q>']
Given exec rejects with non-JSON stdout, runGitHubGraphql rejects with an Error whose cause is the original rejection and whose message contains 'gh api graphql failed (' and no 'query='

The gatherer file contains no 'async function runGitHubGraphql', imports it from './github-graphql-run.js', wc -l reports at most 765 lines, the import-graph guard test still passes, and the new module contains no execSync or spawnSync
Retry the gh GraphQL call once when stdout carries no JSON envelope

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/github-graphql-run.test.ts passes including the fake-timer retry cases

narrative.Action: In src/lib/github-graphql-run.ts turn the single attempt into `for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++)` per PRD WI-2. Rule inside the catch, after the has-data check: if the stdout parsed as a JSON envelope (errors-only) OR attempt > 1, throw the wrapped error; otherwise `await delay(GH_GRAPHQL_RETRY_DELAY_MS)` and loop so the same args run a second time. Add fake-timer tests (vi.useFakeTimers in beforeEach, vi.useRealTimers in afterEach, vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1000)): non-JSON failure then success resolves after one delay(1000) with exec called twice with identical args; two non-JSON failures reject with 'attempt 2'; an errors-only envelope `{"errors":[{"message":"API rate limit exceeded"}],"data":null}` rejects with 'attempt 1' and exec called once and delay never called; vi.getTimerCount() is 0 after resolution. gh-run-stderr's tests assert no attempt number through runGitHubGraphql, so this item only adds tests; the end-to-end attempt-count assertions live here.

items.title: Given exec rejects once with { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: 'error connecting' } then resolves { stdout: '{"data":{}}' }, when timers advance 1000 ms then runGitHubGraphql resolves with the second stdout and exec was called twice with identical args
Given exec rejects twice with non-JSON stdout, the runner rejects with a message containing 'attempt 2' and exec was called exactly twice
Given exec rejects with an errors-only JSON envelope on stdout, the runner rejects with 'attempt 1', exec was called once, and the injected delay was never called

Given fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync), the retry test resolves and vi.getTimerCount() returns 0 afterwards; the default delay wraps the global setTimeout and the module contains no import of node:timers/promises
